definition: A type of recurrent neural network architecture with gating mechanisms designed to better capture long-range dependencies in sequences.
details: LSTMs use input, output, and forget gates to control the flow of information, mitigating the vanishing gradient problem that plagued simple RNNs.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Think of it this way: A type of recurrent neural network architecture with gating mechanisms designed to better capture long-range dependencies in sequences. And here is the clever part: LSTMs use input, output, and forget gates to control the flow of information, mitigating the vanishing gradient problem that plagued simple RNNs. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — Long Short-Term Memory — is what makes everything else possible.
